# CIVILIAN GUIDANCE [italic]Read once. Comply every shift.[/italic]
The detachment's job is to keep this colony, its people and its works intact. On a quiet day you will see a fire team walk past the mess and nothing more. When the Commanding Officer raises the alert state, the rules below apply to everyone: residents, contractors and visitors alike.
## AT A CHECKPOINT - Halt when ordered to halt. Keep your hands visible. - Present your colony ID. Contractors also present a current work order. - Declare any firearm before you are searched. A weapon without a Colonial Marshal licence will be confiscated and logged. - Do not photograph or record checkpoints, sentry posts or troop movements.
## CURFEW - Curfew hours are posted on this board and announced over the colony PA. - Movement after curfew requires a pass from Colony Administration or the detachment duty officer. Essential workers carry theirs on their person.
## WHEN THE SIREN SOUNDS - Get indoors, away from windows, and stay there until the all clear. - Follow your block warden. Do not come to the garrison gate; it will be closed. - Shelter locations are listed by [netlink="Colony Administration" link="admin.colony.gov"].
## REPORT - Unattended bags, crates or vehicles. - Anyone asking about patrol times, the armoury or the landing pad. - Cut fences, broken locks, missing explosives or mining charges. - A gas alarm sounding, or a gas monitor that is dark, damaged or tampered with. Carbon monoxide has no smell. The monitor is your nose.
The Corps does not ask about your politics. It asks that you do not carry a rifle for anyone.
## WHAT MARINES DO NOT DO Marines do not collect debts, settle disputes between neighbours or enforce Company contracts. Take those to the Colonial Marshals or to Administration. A complaint about a Marine goes in writing to the Executive Officer. Every complaint is logged and answered.
